answer: At the yearly summit each household names the one duty it can never discharge itself - a widow's water debt, a ferryman's promise - and conveys it to one address only, never twice. The head must discharge it at the zenith of the pass, where the one creditor waits, and speak the household's own fable of how the debt came to be. The scarce per-head input is that irreplaceable duty and its telling: unprintable, unlendable to a sibling, spent once discharged. A farm's tenth head needs a tenth household, and the roll of discharged duties shows one address holding a column.
